p.src: But all these were only dreams, in reality there was only one thing left to do—to get away as quickly as possible, not to stay another hour in this place. p.src: "No!" said Mashenka resolutely, beginning to tremble. "Let me alone, I entreat you!"

u.src: "No!" said Mashenka resolutely, beginning to tremble.
"Let me alone, I entreat you!"

p.src: "Well, God bless you!" sighed Nikolay Sergeitch, sitting down on the stool near the box. "I must own I like people who still can feel resentment, contempt, and so on. I could sit here forever and look at your indignant face.... So you won't stay, then? I understand.... It's bound to be so ... Yes, of course.... It's all right for you, but for me—wo-o-o-o!... I can't stir a step out of this cellar. I'd go off to one of our estates, but in every one of them there are some of my wife's rascals ... stewards, experts, damn them all! They mortgage and remortgage.... You mustn't catch fish, must keep off the grass, mustn't break the trees."

p.src: "Then you won't stay?" asked Nikolay Sergeitch, getting up quickly and going towards the door. "You might as well stay, really. In the evenings I could come and have a talk with you. Eh? Stay! If you go, there won't be a human face left in the house. It's awful!"
